security_audit.summary: All 25 static findings are false positives caused by documentation syntax, file references, and code review checklist language. No evidence was found of command execution, filesystem access, network reconnaissance, or prompt injection in the four scanned files.

remediation.issue: Static scanning interprets fenced Graphviz diagrams and inline file references as external command execution.
remediation.suggestion: Keep diagrams and file references clearly fenced as documentation, and consider scanner exclusions for Markdown code fences.

remediation.issue: A hypothetical user-level installation path triggers hidden-file access findings.
remediation.suggestion: Label installation paths as examples and document that the skill performs no installation or filesystem writes.

remediation.issue: Checklist language is broad enough to trigger reconnaissance rules.
remediation.suggestion: Retain the review checklist, but use explicit terms such as implementation, repository, and specification when practical.

content.value_statement: Independent implementation tasks can lose context and miss review gates. This skill coordinates fresh subagents, specification checks, and quality reviews for each task.
actual_capabilities: Breaks an implementation plan into independent tasks.
Dispatches a fresh implementer subagent for each task.
Runs specification compliance review before code quality review.
Routes review issues back to the implementer for fixes.
Tracks task completion and performs a final review.
limitations: It requires a clear implementation plan with sufficiently independent tasks.
It does not replace environment-specific validation or expert review.
It is not designed for tightly coupled tasks or parallel implementation conflicts.
It depends on the available subagent and review tools.

use_cases.title: Implement a Feature Plan
use_cases.description: Turn a multi-task engineering plan into reviewed implementation steps with focused context for each task.

use_cases.title: Add Review Gates
use_cases.description: Require specification and code quality checks after each implementation task before marking work complete.

use_cases.title: Improve Repository Changes
use_cases.description: Use fresh task context, test expectations, and review feedback to reduce missed requirements and unnecessary changes.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Simple Task
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to implement one independent task from my plan. Ask questions first, then test the change and report the result.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner workflow for a single clear task.

prompt_templates.title: Review Each Task
prompt_templates.prompt: Execute the independent tasks in this plan. After each task, run specification review, then code quality review, and fix reported issues.
prompt_templates.scenario: Routine feature work with review gates.

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate Test-Driven Work
prompt_templates.prompt: For every task, provide full context to a fresh implementer, require tests, and repeat both reviews until the task passes.

prompt_templates.title: Run the Full Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Execute this plan using fresh subagents, task tracking, implementation tests, two-stage reviews, and a final review of the complete change.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow for a multi-task repository change.

output_examples.input: Implement the first independent task in the approved feature plan.
output_examples.output: Task completed with tests passing. Specification review found no gaps. Code quality review approved the change.

output_examples.input: Run the workflow for a plan with three independent tasks.
output: Task one implemented, tested, and approved by both reviews.
Task two revised after a specification gap, then approved.
Task three completed and included in the final repository review.

output_examples.input: Review the completed implementation before merging.
output_examples.output: The final review confirms that the requested tasks are implemented, tested, and ready for the repository's normal finishing workflow.

best_practices: Provide each subagent with the full task text and relevant repository context.
Complete specification review before starting code quality review.
Require tests, self-review, and a clear report for every completed task.
anti_patterns: Do not dispatch multiple implementation subagents to conflicting files in parallel.
Do not skip a review gate or leave reported issues unresolved.
Do not use this workflow when tasks are tightly coupled or the plan is unclear.

faq.question: What type of work does this skill support?
faq.answer: It supports implementation plans containing tasks that can be completed independently in the current session.

faq.question: What happens after implementation?
faq.answer: A specification reviewer checks requirements first. A code quality reviewer checks maintainability and testing second.

faq.question: Can an implementer ask questions?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow pauses for clarification before implementation when requirements, dependencies, or assumptions are unclear.

faq.question: Does the skill run tests?
faq.answer: It instructs implementers to write and verify tests, but the actual test commands depend on the repository.

faq.question: When should I use another workflow?
faq.answer: Use another workflow for tightly coupled tasks, parallel sessions, missing requirements, or work without an implementation plan.

faq.question: Does this skill make changes automatically?
faq.answer: It coordinates subagents that may implement and commit changes. Review the proposed work and repository policy before merging.
